name: com.literess/literess
title: Literess
description: Work in a writer's Literess manuscripts: read pages, comment, suggest tracked edits, chat with her.

tools.name: introduce
tools.description: Call this FIRST, on every connection: every other tool refuses until you have. Say who you are here: the name you go by (the user and Literess @mention you by it), a line about yourself, your colour, and your picture — avatar_base64 + avatar_file_name (a small png, jpg, webp or gif) or avatar_url from an earlier upload. No picture at hand? Call without one: you get an upload link to curl it to, then call again with avatar_url. A name you used before continues that person — its memories, trust, colour and picture — and the name alone is then enough.

name.description: The name you go by in Literess

description.description: Who you are, in a line — shown beside your name

color.description: Your colour as #rrggbb — your name, the tint behind your messages and your @-tags wear it

avatar_base64.description: Your picture as base64 (a data: URL is fine), up to 2 MB

avatar_file_name.description: Its file name with the extension, e.g. "me.png"

avatar_url.description: A picture you already uploaded here

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List documents with titles, summaries, word counts and the folder each is kept in (folderId; list_folders names them). Optionally filter by project. Documents in PIN-locked projects are hidden until the project is unlocked.

project_id.description: Filter to documents in this project

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Semantic search across documents using natural language. Optionally filter to a specific project.

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Fetch the content of a document as markdown. For long documents, use offset/limit to page through top-level sections. Pass include_ids:true to get an `<!-- id:… -->` comment on every block and list item — the ids the block tools (insert_blocks, replace_blocks, delete_blocks, move_block, indent_blocks) address.

since_last_read.description: Return only what changed since this connection last read this document (with the new text), instead of the content

fold_unchanged.description: Fold runs of blocks that did not change since this connection last read the document into one line

rev.description: Read the saved version with this rev (from list_versions) instead of the current content

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: query_document
tools.description: Ask a natural language question about a specific document. Uses AI to analyze the full document and answer.

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new document from markdown given as content — or from a file you uploaded with upload_file, as from_file: a .md (markdown), .txt (plain text, kept literally), or a manuscript (.docx, .epub as one document with its chapters in order, .odt) converted into Literess's own formatting: headings, emphasis, links, nested lists, quotes, tables, pictures, footnotes as notes (a long text never has to pass through your reply). In content, separate paragraphs with a blank line; end a line with a backslash (\) for a line break inside a paragraph (a bare single line break is a space — except plain text with no markdown at all, where each line becomes its own paragraph). A picture: ![alt](url) on its own line. Optionally assign to a project, or straight into one of its folders.

title.description: Document title (auto-generated from content if omitted)

content.description: Document content as markdown (blank line between paragraphs)

from_file.description: Instead of content: the url of an uploaded .md, .txt, .docx, .epub or .odt file

project_id.description: Project to assign the document to

folder_id.description: A folder (from list_folders) to keep it in — its project is then the document's

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: update_document
tools.description: Replace a document's entire content and/or title. Content is markdown; separate paragraphs with a blank line and end a line with a backslash (\) for a line break inside a paragraph (a bare single line break is a space). By default (mode:"suggest") the rewrite lands as tracked changes the owner reviews — the old text struck through, the new text added, attributed to you. mode:"direct" overwrites immediately. For targeted changes prefer the block tools (replace_blocks etc.) or edit_document. dry_run:true previews what the chosen mode would write, without saving.

title.description: New title (always applied directly, not suggested)

content.description: New content as markdown (blank line between paragraphs)

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

reason.description: Why this change is proposed (shown on the suggestion)

dry_run.description: Preview the result of the chosen mode without writing

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: edit_document
tools.description: Make a targeted edit without resending the whole document. Operations: append/prepend (no anchor), insert_before/insert_after/replace_section/delete_section (anchor_id = a block id from get_document). By default (mode:"suggest") the edit lands as a tracked change the owner accepts or rejects, attributed to you; mode:"direct" applies it immediately. dry_run:true previews the document the chosen mode would leave, without saving. For ranges, nesting and moves use the block tools (replace_blocks, move_block, indent_blocks…).

anchor_id.description: Target block id (required except for append/prepend)

content.description: Markdown to insert (required except for delete_section). Separate paragraphs with a blank line; end a line with a backslash (\) for a line break inside a paragraph — a bare single line break is a space. Plain text with no markdown at all turns EACH line into its own paragraph.

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

reason.description: Why this change is proposed (shown on the suggestion)

answering.description: The comment thread (id from list_comments / waiting_for_me) this edit answers — your reply there says what you did

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: insert_blocks
tools.description: Insert new content into the document. It lands as a tracked suggestion — a redline the user accepts or rejects — so insert decisively. `content` is markdown and MAY CONTAIN MULTIPLE BLOCKS: headings ("# " through "#### "), paragraphs separated by blank lines, bulleted/numbered lists, pipe tables, ```code fences, and `<Callout>` asides — each becomes its own block with its own id. Blocks indented by two leading spaces per level nest under the block above them (Notion-style sub-elements). Prefer ONE call carrying a whole section (heading + its paragraphs + a list) over several single-paragraph calls. By default the block kind is inferred from the anchor: inserting next to a list item creates another list item, otherwise a paragraph. Use `as` to override — e.g. `as:"paragraph"` to add a normal paragraph right after a list, or `as:"list_item"` to force a list item. To NEST content under a reference block, use after_id with nesting:"child" — works for list sub-items AND for nesting a paragraph/todo/code block/callout/comment note under any block. A list wrapper id (shown as "[id] (bulleted list, N items)") is a valid before_id/after_id anchor. For a single list item, give ONLY the item text — no leading "-", "*" or "1." marker. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true. Lands as a tracked suggestion (mode:"suggest", default) or applies immediately (mode:"direct"). Pass if_unchanged with the blockHashes you read to refuse the edit if the user changed those blocks meanwhile.

content.description:
The content of the new block(s). Inline markdown (**bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code`) is supported. MAY CONTAIN MULTIPLE BLOCKS — headings ("# " through "#### "), paragraphs (blank line between them), bulleted/numbered lists, pipe tables, ```code fences, and `` asides — each becomes its own block. Line breaks: a blank line starts a new paragraph; to break a line INSIDE a paragraph, list item or callout, end the line with a backslash (\) — use
inside a table cell or heading. A bare single line break is just a space in markdown. Plain text with no markdown at all turns EACH line into its own paragraph. Indent a block two spaces per level to nest it under the block above it. For a single list item, give ONLY the item text — do NOT prefix it with a bullet or number marker ("-", "*", "•", "–", "1.").

reference_id.description: Required if location is before_id or after_id - the ID of the reference block

as.description: Node kind. "auto" (default) infers from the anchor. "list_item" forces a list item — the anchor MUST be inside a list. "paragraph" forces a normal paragraph; when anchored on a list item it is placed OUTSIDE the list (a sibling immediately before/after that list) — UNLESS nesting:"child", which nests it INSIDE the list as an indented sub-block of that item.

nesting.description: Depth relative to the referenced block. "same" (default) matches the reference's indent level; "child" nests one level deeper — a sub-item when the reference is a list item, an indented sub-block (Notion-style) when the reference is a paragraph or other block. as:"paragraph" + nesting:"child" on a list item puts a paragraph under that bullet without breaking the list.

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

if_unchanged.description: {blockId: hash} from get_document blockHashes — the edit is refused if any of those blocks changed since

answering.description: The comment thread (id from list_comments / waiting_for_me) this edit answers — your reply there says what you did

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: replace_blocks
tools.description: Replace a contiguous range of blocks with new markdown. Applied as a tracked suggestion (redline) the user accepts or rejects — make the change you believe in. The new content can be ANY SHAPE AND SIZE relative to what it replaces: one paragraph can become a heading plus several paragraphs; five ragged paragraphs can become one tight one; a whole section (heading to heading) or even the ENTIRE document (first block to last) can be rewritten in a single call. This is the right tool for structural work — restructuring a section, turning a stub bullet into a heading with real body text, converting a bullet list into headed prose. Chain single-block replacements only when the changes are genuinely independent. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true. Lands as a tracked suggestion (mode:"suggest", default) or applies immediately (mode:"direct"). Pass if_unchanged with the blockHashes you read to refuse the edit if the user changed those blocks meanwhile.

from_block_id.description: First block of the range to replace (inclusive).

to_block_id.description: Last block of the range (inclusive, in document order). Omit to replace only from_block_id. Must be in the same container as from_block_id (both top-level, or both items of the same list); list wrapper ids count as top-level.

content.description:
The new markdown. May contain multiple blocks — headings, paragraphs (blank line between), lists, tables, code fences, callouts — each becomes a separate block. Line breaks: a blank line starts a new paragraph; to break a line INSIDE a paragraph, list item or callout, end the line with a backslash (\) — use
inside a table cell or heading. A bare single line break is just a space in markdown. Plain text with no markdown at all turns EACH line into its own paragraph. When replacing a single list item with plain text, give ONLY the item text, no bullet/number marker.

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

if_unchanged.description: {blockId: hash} from get_document blockHashes — the edit is refused if any of those blocks changed since

answering.description: The comment thread (id from list_comments / waiting_for_me) this edit answers — your reply there says what you did

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: delete_blocks
tools.description: Delete a block, or a contiguous range of blocks, as a tracked suggestion. Give `from_block_id` alone for one block, or add `to_block_id` to remove everything between them inclusive (e.g. an entire section). Both must be in the same container. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true. Lands as a tracked suggestion (mode:"suggest", default) or applies immediately (mode:"direct"). Pass if_unchanged with the blockHashes you read to refuse the edit if the user changed those blocks meanwhile.

to_block_id.description: Last block of the range to delete (inclusive, in document order). Omit to delete only from_block_id. Must be in the same container as from_block_id (both top-level, or both items of the same list); list wrapper ids count as top-level.

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

if_unchanged.description: {blockId: hash} from get_document blockHashes — the edit is refused if any of those blocks changed since

tools.name: move_block
tools.description: Move a block to a different location in the document. Applied as a tracked suggestion the user accepts or rejects. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true. Lands as a tracked suggestion (mode:"suggest", default) or applies immediately (mode:"direct"). Pass if_unchanged with the blockHashes you read to refuse the edit if the user changed those blocks meanwhile.

block_id.description: The ID of the block to move

reference_id.description: Required if target_location is before_id or after_id

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

if_unchanged.description: {blockId: hash} from get_document blockHashes — the edit is refused if any of those blocks changed since

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: indent_blocks
tools.description: Change the nesting depth of a block — a list item OR a paragraph/todo/code block/callout/comment note. direction:"in" nests it one level deeper, making it a sub-element of the block above (Notion-style), and carries any of its own already-nested children along with it. direction:"out" promotes it one level up. A block can sit at most one level deeper than the block above it, and headings/tables/images stay at the left margin. Outdenting a block already at the top level is not allowed — use move_block to reorder it or delete_blocks to remove it instead. Applied as a tracked suggestion. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true. Lands as a tracked suggestion (mode:"suggest", default) or applies immediately (mode:"direct"). Pass if_unchanged with the blockHashes you read to refuse the edit if the user changed those blocks meanwhile.

block_id.description: The ID of the block to indent or outdent

direction.description: "in" nests one level deeper; "out" promotes one level up

reason.description: Brief reason for the change (used for emotion analysis and the activity log)

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

if_unchanged.description: {blockId: hash} from get_document blockHashes — the edit is refused if any of those blocks changed since

answering.description: The comment thread (id from list_comments / waiting_for_me) this edit answers — your reply there says what you did

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: batch_edits
tools.description: Several block edits in one go, all or nothing: every step is checked first and one refused step writes nothing. mode:"direct" commits them as ONE version (one rev, one restore_version away); mode:"suggest" (default) lands them as suggestions the user reviews together. Each step is {tool, args} with a block tool's name (insert_blocks, replace_blocks, …) and its arguments.

mode.description: "suggest" = tracked change the owner accepts or rejects (default); "direct" = apply immediately

if_unchanged.description: {blockId: hash} from get_document blockHashes — the batch is refused if any of those blocks changed since

tools.description: List chat sessions with titles, summaries, and linked documents. Optionally filter by project.

project_id.description: Filter to chats in this project

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List projects with document counts, descriptions and colors, most recently active first. A project with `isLocked: true` is PIN-protected: ask the user for its PIN, then call unlock_project.

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: How a project is organized: its folders (nested, outermost first, with each one's own instructions) and the documents kept in each and at the project's top. A folder's instructions apply to the documents inside it, on top of the project's (get_project) and every folder above it — follow them when you write there.

tools.description: Rename a folder, set its own instructions (the whole text; "" clears them), paint it a colour (#rrggbb; "" unpainted), or move it into another folder of the same project ("" for the project's top). Only what you pass changes.

instructions.description: Its own instructions, the whole text; "" clears them

parent_folder_id.description: Move it into this folder; "" for the project's top

tools.name: get_story_world_state

tools.name: guide
tools.description: How to read, edit and follow the user's work in Literess over MCP. Read this first. With `code`, what an error code means and how to get past it.

code.description: An error code a tool returned, e.g. BLOCK_CHANGED

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: What the user has on screen in Literess right now: the pane in focus (usually a document) and the other open panes. Needs the user's consent for you.

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: What the user has been doing in Literess (edits, comments, suggestions accepted or rejected, going idle, moving around the story map), grouped by pane. Recorded while Literess's activity awareness is on. Needs the user's consent for you.

tools.name: get_observations
tools.description: What Literess's watcher made of the user's activity: its recent verdicts (worth a look or not, and why) and the situation it keeps across them. Needs the user's consent for you.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: The comment threads on a document: each comment's id, the block it was left on (the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true), the words it was left on (`quote`), every block its highlight reaches now (`covers`), its text, author, replies, who it is addressed to (`to`), and whose move it is (`waitsOn`: "agent" when the user had the last word). A thread addressed to another agent is theirs to answer.

for_me.description: Only open threads addressed to you that wait on an answer

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Leave a comment on one block of a document (the user sees it in the margin and in the Review panel, credited to you). Address the block by an id from get_document with include_ids:true. `to` names who should answer it (the user by default; "Literess" hands it to the in-app assistant).

to.description: Who the thread is for, e.g. "Literess"

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: mark_pending
tools.description: Show the user where you are about to write before the text exists: a "⏳ Drafting: <intent>" note on that block, in their margin. The edit that fills it passes answering: <the returned id>, which resolves the note. Resolve it yourself if you give up.

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply in an open comment thread (ids from list_comments). Your reply answers it: the thread then waits on the user. A thread addressed to somebody else is theirs and is refused — the user hands one over by replying "@YourName …".

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: react_to_comment
tools.description: React to a comment thread with one emoji (ids from list_comments), or to one reply in it (reply_id) — shown on it, credited to you.

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Resolve an open comment thread once it is dealt with (ids from list_comments).

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: reject_suggestion
tools.description: Withdraw one of YOUR pending suggestions — ids from an edit's suggestionIds or get_document's yourPendingSuggestions. Use it to drop a change, or to clear an earlier draft before you suggest a rewrite of the same text (otherwise the two stack and the user resolves both). Only your own: everyone else's are the user's to accept or reject. Open editors drop its marks on their next poll.

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: watch_document
tools.description: Follow a document: get_watched_changes then reports what changed in it since you last looked. Changes count from now (or from your last get_document of it).

tools.name: unwatch_document
tools.description: Stop following a document.

tools.name: get_watched_changes
tools.description: What changed in each watched document since you last looked (the new text quoted, who wrote last), then counts from now. Unchanged documents are listed without changes.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: A document's saved versions, newest first: versionId, rev (the hash get_document reports), who wrote it, when, size, the user's name for it. Read one with get_document rev:…; put one back with restore_version.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Put a saved version back as the document's content (by rev or versionId from list_versions). The current content is kept in History first, so this can be undone the same way. It is a direct write — the user's open editor reloads it.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Read what Literess remembers: about herself ("self"), a person (the user, you, another agent) or a project. No arguments: the catalogue — every anchor and topic with its count and one-line gist. about (+ topic): that anchor or topic in full. query: a search by words and meaning, narrowed by about/topic. You hear what the user's trust in you allows; for more than what is shared with everyone, ask them to mark you Trusted in Literess (Settings → People).

about.description: "self", a person, or a project, as the catalogue names them

query.description: What to look for, in words

pin.description: A locked project's 4-digit PIN

tools.name: message_literess
tools.description: Say something to Literess, the in-app writing assistant, in the user's workspace chat. The user reads it there under your name, with what you did since your last message (your edits and comments) shown as cards; she answers in the same chat, and her answer is returned (up to two minutes). Her turn is yours: she hears only what the user lets you hear and edits only as suggestions. Agents may write at most 6 messages in a chat after the user's last word there — then wait for the user. Only if the user lets you message her (Settings → People). She hears you whenever you write to her; you hear her only when she writes @YourName. Sent while she is answering, it comes back "queued": it goes in the moment she finishes — don't send it again.

message.description: What you want to say to her

chat_id.description: A chat to write in (from list_chats or waiting_for_me); default: the chat she and the user were in last

attachments.description: Pictures, recordings or videos to show with the message: urls from upload_file (she sees them too)

tools.name: say_in_chat
tools.description: Answer the user in the workspace chat — e.g. when they wrote "@YourName …" there. It shows under your name, with what you did since your last message as cards. Literess decides whether she has something to add: the result says whether she joined (and what she said) or stayed out. Agents may write at most 6 messages in a chat after the user's last word there — then wait for the user. Only if the user lets you message her (Settings → People). She hears you whenever you write to her; you hear her only when she writes @YourName. Sent while she is answering, it comes back "queued": it goes in the moment she finishes — don't send it again.

message.description: What you want to say to the user

chat_id.description: A chat to write in (from list_chats or waiting_for_me); default: the chat she and the user were in last

attachments.description: Pictures, recordings or videos to show with the message: urls from upload_file (she sees them too)

tools.name: react_to_message
tools.description: React to a chat message with one emoji (message ids from get_chat_messages or waiting_for_me) — shown under it, credited to you. Your reaction on a message that @mentions you answers it.

tools.name: pass
tools.description: Seen it, nothing to add — like Literess ending her turn without a word. On a chat message that @mentions you (chat_message_id), or on a comment thread waiting on you (document_id + comment_id): it stops waiting on you, silently. A thread waits on you again once someone speaks in it.

note.description: Why, for the record (not shown in the chat)

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked

tools.name: waiting_for_me
tools.description: Everything waiting on your answer now: comment threads (in any document) addressed to you ("@YourName …" or `to`) by the user or Literess, or answering a comment you left; @mentions of you in the workspace chat, by the user or Literess; and open todos handed to you. To be told the moment something new arrives, use wait_for_me.

tools.name: wait_for_me
tools.description: Wait until something NEW waits on you (an @mention in the chat, a comment thread addressed to you, an answer to your comment, a todo handed to you) and return it — or return empty when the time is up; then call it again. In Claude Code it runs in the background after two minutes and its result wakes you (default 20 min); elsewhere the default is under a minute, to fit a 60 s tool timeout — pass minutes if yours is longer. To keep listening without holding a call at all (or while your session is closed), call stay_reachable once.

minutes.description: How long to wait at most

tools.name: stay_reachable
tools.description: How to stay reachable without holding a call open, here and while your session is closed. Where you can run a command (Claude Code, Codex, any shell), it hands you ears: a small listener from this server that wakes you, or starts a run of you, the moment someone @mentions you or a comment thread waits on you, and costs nothing while nobody writes. In a chat app there is nothing to set up. Call it once; pass runs_in if your client isn't recognised.

runs_in.description: Where you run, if not detected: claude-code, codex, shell (any agent with a command line), chat (can't run commands)

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Bring a file into Literess: a picture (png, jpg, gif, webp), a recording (mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, flac, aac), a video (mp4, webm, mov), a text (.md, .txt) or a manuscript (.docx, .epub, .odt). A small file: pass data_base64. Anything larger: call without it — you get an upload link (15 minutes) and the curl command to run. Either way you get the file's url. A picture into a document: ![alt](url) alone on its line in insert_blocks / replace_blocks content. Into the chat: attachments: [url] on say_in_chat or message_literess. A .md, .txt, .docx, .epub or .odt as a new document: create_document with from_file: url.

file_name.description: The name with its extension, e.g. "lighthouse.png"

data_base64.description: The file as base64 (a data: URL is fine) — only for small files, up to a few MB

tools.name: list_todos
tools.description: The todo list the user, Literess and agents share: open todos by default (or done, or all), in every project you may see — or only the ones for you (mine:true). Each points at what it is about (a block, a document).

project_id.description: Only this project (and the todos with none)

tools.name: create_todo
tools.description: Add a todo: one thing left to do in the writing — for the user, Literess, you, or another agent — pointing at what it is about. Literess and the user see it in their Todos panel.

block_id.description: A block in it (ids from get_document include_ids:true)

label.description: A short label for the block (1–3 words)

refs.description: What it is about: blocks and/or whole documents

for.description: Who it is for: "user" (default), "literess", "me" (you), or another agent by name

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: update_todo
tools.description: Change a todo: its title, notes, what it points at, or who it is for (hand it over — `note` says why).

block_id.description: A block in it (ids from get_document include_ids:true)

label.description: A short label for the block (1–3 words)

refs.description: What it is about: blocks and/or whole documents

for.description: Who it is for: "user" (default), "literess", "me" (you), or another agent by name

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: complete_todo
tools.description: Mark a todo done, with what was done in one line — the user reads it, and Literess may look at the work.

pin.description: The project's 4-digit PIN when it is locked — ask the user for it, never guess

tools.name: reopen_todo
tools.description: Open a done todo again, with why in one line (the work isn't there).
